intro.title: Welcome to Oualidia — lagoon and oysters
intro.p1: Oualidia sits on Morocco's Atlantic coast between El Jadida and Safi, built around a long lagoon sheltered from the open ocean. It is best known for oyster farming, seafood tables and a slower pace than the bigger beach resorts.
intro.p2: The town is compact: lagoon walks, oyster tasting, a beach strip and birdlife at the edges. Plan one or two nights if you want lagoon time, a meal of oysters and a rest on the road between Casablanca/El Jadida and Safi or Essaouira.

lagoon.title: The lagoon
lagoon.p1: Oualidia's lagoon is the reason the town exists as a destination. Sheltered from the open Atlantic, it shifts with the tide — calm water, oyster parks and long horizontal light at the end of the day.
lagoon.p2: Walk the banks, watch the working boats and stay for sunset. Swimming depends on season and local advice; the lagoon is more about atmosphere than a classic resort beach.
lagoon.tip: Late afternoon is the most photogenic. Bring wind protection in winter.

oysters.title: Oyster beds & tasting
oysters.p1: Oualidia is one of Morocco's best-known spots for oysters. Farms sit in the lagoon; restaurants and simple tables serve them fresh, often with a view of the water.
oysters.p2: Ask what is in season and how it is harvested. Combine a tasting with a lagoon walk rather than treating it as a standalone stop.
oysters.tip: Lunch by the lagoon is the classic pattern. Book ahead in peak weekends.

beach.title: Beach & dunes
beach.p1: Beyond the lagoon, sandy beaches and dune edges face the open Atlantic. Conditions vary with swell; this is not always a gentle swimming coast.
beach.p2: Good for walks and space. Check local advice before swimming and respect private or working areas near the oyster parks.
beach.tip: Morning or late day for softer light and fewer people.

birds.title: Birdlife & wetland edges
birds.p1: The lagoon and wetland margins attract seasonal birds — a quiet bonus for travellers who like to move slowly with binoculars.
birds.p2: You do not need a formal reserve: the edges of the lagoon and quieter tracks already offer sightings, especially outside peak heat.
birds.tip: Early morning is best. Keep distance from nests and working farms.

viewpoint.title: Lagoon viewpoints
viewpoint.p1: A few roadsides and low rises above the lagoon give the full curve of water, oyster parks and Atlantic light in one frame.
viewpoint.p2: Stop briefly on the approach roads or walk a short way up from the centre — no ticketed viewpoint is required.
viewpoint.tip: Golden hour rewards a short climb or pull-over.

village.title: Village centre
village.p1: Oualidia's centre is small and practical: cafés, a few shops and the base for lagoon restaurants and stays.
village.p2: Use it for coffee, orientation and evening meals rather than a long sightseeing circuit.
village.tip: Everything is walkable once you are in town.

q1.question: How long should I stay in Oualidia?
q1.answer: One night covers lagoon walks and oysters; two nights if you want beach time and a slower pace.

q2.question: Is Oualidia only about oysters?
q2.answer: Oysters are the signature, but the lagoon landscape, birdlife and quiet beaches are the fuller reason to stop.

q3.question: How do I get to Oualidia?
q3.answer: By road from Casablanca or El Jadida (about 2.5–3.5h from CMN depending on stops). Grands taxis and buses serve the coast; a car is flexible for the lagoon and beaches.

q4.question: Can you swim in the lagoon?
q4.answer: Conditions vary with tide and season. Many visitors focus on walks, views and seafood rather than swimming; ask locally before entering the water.
